name: Phupha
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp. Sec. 4.5 'The Downriver meso-clade of Riverine Phula', p. 15.
catalog_quote: The Downriver meso-clade of Riverine Phula includes Phupa [ypp], Phuza [ypz], Phupha [yph] and Alugu [aub]. In addition to sharing in the Riverine Phula innovations and lacking the key Upriver innovations reviewed in the previous section, these languages feature a number of their own exclusive innovations. One involves TC-1 shifting to /21/ with splits to /33/ conditioned by reflexes of *ʔ - and *Cpr *onsets. Another involves high-tone /55/ reflexes of the Riverine *checked-tone merger, with shifts to high-falling /52/ in Alugu, and with few intermediate splits. A TC-2 split to low-rising /13/, conditioned by reflexes of *b,*z, *r and *Cr *onsets is also notable.

new_statements.relation_note: Tone values /21 33 55 13/ attested for Phupha via clade innovations; silent on stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Phupha is a lexical-tone (Ngwi) language: Proto-Ngwi tone class 1 surfaces as low-falling /21/ with conditioned splits to mid /33/, the Riverine checked-tone merger surfaces as high /55/, and tone class 2 shows a conditioned split to low-rising /13/ (Phupha form cited: ȵ̥i13 ma21 'stomach'). No synchronic count of Phupha tonemes is given and nothing is said about word stress or accent anywhere in the work.
new_statements.exceptions: Alugu (sister lect) has /52/ instead of /55/ for the checked-tone merger; Phupa lacks the *voiceless-fricative conditioning of the TC-1 /33/ split that Phupha, Phuza and Alugu share.
new_statements.identity_note: PASS-1/BIBLIOGRAPHY WORK (held, already read; our reader paraphrased this passage but no statement was put held by the project), added: verbatim tone quotation + locator. The passage names 'Phupha [yph]' explicitly (Pelkey is the ISO proposer of yph; his Phupha datapoint is FKC Fengkou, Jiasha, Gejiu = phup1237). In Glottolog the work is filed under the five column languages / down1239, not under phup1237 itself. It is a clade-level diachronic statement (Phupa, Phuza, Phupha, Alugu together), not a synchronic Phupha sketch; the book's five 'phonology in brief' sketches exclude Phupha.
